title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced a shared initial candidate and, when invoked, a guarded final artifact after validator + repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute reduction = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. We correct prior labeling ambiguities by (1) defining contingency-cell notation and mapping to archived CSVs, (2) explaining provider-call accounting and why model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair), and (3) publishing full artifact SHA-256 digests referenced in the Disclosure Statement for unambiguous forensic inspection.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are widely proposed for translating human intent into device-specific network configurations. Operational deployments typically layer deterministic validators and automated repairs as guardrails, but rigorous preregistered quantification of the marginal reduction in actionable misconfiguration is limited. Research question. After an autonomy-locked preregistration we asked: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and which residual error types remain after automated repairs? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001) executed end-to-end with archived artifacts and cryptographic hashes; (2) a corrected, artifact-grounded report resolving contingency-cell and provider-call accounting ambiguities raised in review; (3) a null/near-null confirmatory outcome for the chosen model/validator/task bank and explicit limits on what that outcome implies operationally.
sections.related_work: We position this study among work on deterministic network verification (e.g., header-space analysis and incremental checkers) and recent LLM→NetOps evaluations and prototypes (e.g., NetConfEval and intent-driven configuration studies). We relied on verified primary sources when designing the validator-backed guard and the paired estimand. Unlike broad model-leaderboard papers, our contribution is a tightly preregistered, artifact-backed confirmatory test of marginal ROI from a deterministic validator + limited automated repair budget under a paired design.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) froze the paired binary design (N=200 tasks, stratified across vendor families) and analysis plan before execution. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory H1 required ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate. Execution contract. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Budget: maximum_model_calls = 400; actual model_calls_used recorded = 201. Generation semantics and provider-call accounting (clarification). The preregistered contract used a shared initial candidate per task (independent_condition_generation = false). Concretely: the pipeline produced one shared_initial generation per task (200 shared_initial generations across 200 tasks). The baseline scoring labels apply to that shared initial candidate. The guarded condition is defined as the final artifact after validator+repair when the adapter invoked repair; if repair was not invoked the guarded artifact equals the shared initial candidate. Provider-call accounting therefore shows stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1} and condition_counts = {"shared": 200, "guarded": 1}; this means that the hosted model was called 200 times to produce shared_initial candidates and a single additional hosted-model repair call occurred (total hosted_model_call_event_count = 201), which explains model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair. Validator and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applied full intent-constraint validation and simulator-based semantic checks producing per-task JSON traces archived under execution/scoring/. Missingness and exclusions. The preregistered missingness/retry policy was followed; no model-call failures occurred and complete_pairs = 200.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 on archived scoring JSONs (input results SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (baseline success rate = 0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (guarded success rate = 1.000). Absolute paired reduction (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Discordant-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) are: n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Contingency-cell notation and explicit mapping (required correction). We define and use the contingency-cell notation consistent with the archived CSV header 'guarded,baseline,count' (rows are guarded first, baseline second):
- n_11: count where guarded=1 and baseline=1 (both conditions valid).
- n_10: count where guarded=1 and baseline=0 (guarded valid but baseline invalid) — an improvement attributable to the repair/guard.
- n_01: count where guarded=0 and baseline=1 (guarded invalid but baseline valid) — a deterioration.
- n_00: count where guarded=0 and baseline=0 (both invalid).
In our run the single discordant cell is n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0). The analysis JSON field discordant_ordering explicitly records the mapping used: 'n_10=guarded_only;n_01=baseline_only'. Statistical tests. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the absolute reduction = [0.0, 0.015] (bootstrap resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Secondary preregistered hypothesis (H2) untestable. Because guarded residual actionable failures = 0 (n_00 + n_01 = 0), the preregistered confirmatory contingency test for H2 (residual error-type proportions) could not be executed; any error-type discussion is therefore exploratory only. Forensic pointers. The discordant episode and all per-task scoring JSONs are archived under execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and execution/scoring/. Auditors can filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for the pair with guarded=1 and baseline=0 to obtain the exact episode id and then inspect execution/scoring/<episode>-baseline.json and execution/scoring/<episode>-guarded.json for the validator traces.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under the constrained experimental conditions (synthetic task bank, single hosted model gpt-5-mini, single deterministic validator implementation, and an adapter-enforced single-repair budget), the guarded pipeline yielded only a numerically small absolute reduction because the baseline LLM-generated actionable-error prevalence was already very low (1/200). Operational implications. Deterministic validators are valuable for canonicalization, auditing, and surfacing systematic errors; their operational ROI (reduced human review, outage avoidance) depends strongly on baseline generator accuracy, validator coverage, repair budget, and human-in-the-loop costs. Study limitations that affect interpretation. (a) Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; no multi-model generality is implied. (b) Synthetic benchmark and validator scope: task realism and validator semantics bound external validity. (c) Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes. (d) Repair budget: adapter limited repairs to one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair regimes are unexplored. (e) Secondary hypothesis untestable: because guarded residual failures = 0 we could not run the preregistered confirmatory contingency test for H2; this is reported transparently. Reproducibility. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts referenced above are archived with SHA-256 checksums and explicit file paths (see Disclosure Statement).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment of a deterministic-validator guard for LLM→NetOps generate→verify→repair pipelines. On the chosen synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator/repair adapter (≤1 repair), the absolute actionable-misconfiguration reduction was 0.005 (from 1/200 to 0/200). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. We corrected contingency-cell labeling and clarified provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair, and contingency CSV ordering is 'guarded,baseline,count' with n_10 defined above as guarded-only improvements. All artifacts and SHA-256 digests required for forensic audit are listed in the Disclosure Statement. Future work should expand model coverage, validator implementations, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair yields material operational risk reduction.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.
